subject: math
title: Position and Directions: Left, Right and Moves on a Grid
seo_title: Grade 1 Position and Directions Worksheets: Left, Right and Maps (Free)
standard_text: Give and follow directions for moving from one location to another
meta_desc: Free Grade 1 math worksheets on position and directions for the Ontario curriculum: above, below, beside, between, in front of and behind, left and right, following moves like 2 squares right and 1 up on a grid, and finding the way on a classroom map. 100 picture questions with an answer key.
key_big: Count the moves, not the square you start on.
key_sub: Left is the side of your left hand. Right is the side of your right hand. Do the first move, then the second move.
body_html:
Where is it?

Position words tell us where something is.

Between means in the middle of two things.

Left and right

Left is the side of your left hand. Right is the side of your right hand. Look at the picture from where you sit.

Follow moves on a grid

Move one square at a time. Say each number as you move.

Count the moves, not the square you start on.

Which way to the carpet?

Example 1

Zoe stands in front of Owen in a line. Where is Owen?

Zoe is closer to the front. Owen is further back.

Answer: behind Zoe

Example 2

Maya is 2 squares to the left of the easel. Which way does she go?

The easel is on her right side. Count the moves: 1, 2.

Answer: 2 squares right

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Mixing up left and rightHold up your hands. Your left hand makes an L shape
Counting the start squareCount the moves: 1, 2, 3 …
Mixing up up and downUp is toward the top of the page
Saying on when it is aboveOn touches. Above has a gap
Doing the moves in the wrong orderDo the first move, then the second move

faq.q: What do Grade 1 students learn about position and directions in Ontario math?
faq.a: In the Ontario curriculum (Spatial Sense, E1.4 and E1.5), Grade 1 students describe where things are with words like above, below, beside, between, in front of, behind, left and right. They also give and follow directions to move from one place to another.

faq.q: How can I help my child learn left and right?
faq.a: Hold up both hands, fingers up and thumbs out. The left hand makes an L shape. Play “touch your left ear” and say left and right on the walk to school.

faq.q: What are good direction games for Grade 1?
faq.a: Play “robot”: one child gives directions like “3 steps forward, then 2 steps right” and the other follows. A treasure hunt to the carpet or the cubbies works well too.

faq.q: Why does my child get one square too many or too few?
faq.a: Many children count the square they start on. Show them to count each move instead: touch the next square and say 1, then 2, and so on.

sets.title: Above, below, beside, between, in front of, behind

items.q: Where is the beaver?
items.e: The beaver is on the table. It touches the table top. Above would have a gap.

items.q: Where is the ball?
items.e: The ball is under the table. It is below the table top.

items.q: Where is the balloon?
items.e: The balloon is above the table. It is higher than the table, with a gap. It does not touch the table, so it is not on it.

items.q: Where is the duck?
items.e: The duck is beside the table. It is at the side, close by.

items.q: Where is the teddy?
items.e: The teddy is on the table. It touches the table top. Above would have a gap.

items.q: Where is the cat?
items.e: The cat is under the table. It is below the table top.

items.q: Where is the beaver?
items.e: The box hides part of the beaver. The beaver is further back. It is behind the box.

items.q: Where is the ball?
items.e: We can see all of the ball. It is closer to us than the box. It is in front of the box.

items.q: Where is the teddy?
items.e: We can see all of the teddy. It is closer to us than the box. It is in front of the box.

items.q: Where is the duck?
items.e: The box hides part of the duck. The duck is further back. It is behind the box.

items.q: What is between the teddy and the ball?
items.e: Between means in the middle. The beaver is in the middle.

items.q: What is between the duck and the car?
items.e: Find the duck and the car. The mitt is in the middle of them.

items.q: Where is the book?
c: between the cat and the duck
items.e: The cat is on one side. The duck is on the other side. The book is between them.

items.q: What is just above the beaver?
items.e: Look up from the beaver. The star is on the shelf above. The cat is below.

items.q: What is just below the star?
items.e: Look down from the star. The mitt is on the shelf below. The car is above.

items.q: Where is the apple?
items.e: The apple is on the top shelf. The teddy is on the shelf under it. The apple is above the teddy.

items.q: Where is the star?
items.e: The star is on the bottom shelf. The duck is on the shelf over it. The star is below the duck.

items.q: Which picture shows the duck under the table?
items.e: Picture A. The duck is below the table top. In one picture a ball is under the table, not the duck.

items.q: Which picture shows the beaver behind the box?
items.e: Picture B. The box hides part of the beaver. So the beaver is behind the box.

items.q: Which picture shows the balloon above the table?
items.e: Picture D. The balloon is higher than the table. There is a gap.

items.q: Which toy is at the left end?
items.e: Left is the side of your left hand. The beaver is at the left end.

items.q: Which toy is at the right end?
items.e: Right is the side of your right hand. The cat is at the right end.

items.q: Which toy is at the right end?
items.e: Right is the side of your right hand. The ball is at the right end. The duck is at the left end.

items.q: Which toy is at the left end?
items.e: Left is the side of your left hand. The car is at the left end.

items.q: Which toy is 2nd from the left?
items.e: Start at the left end. Count 1, 2: the teddy, the duck. The 2nd toy is the duck. The beaver is 2nd from the right.

items.q: Which toy is 2nd from the right?
items.e: Start at the right end. Count 1, 2: the book, the duck. The 2nd toy is the duck. The apple is 2nd from the left.

items.q: Which toy is 3rd from the left?
items.e: Start at the left end. Count 1, 2, 3: the ball, the mitt, the star. The 3rd toy is the star. The teddy is 3rd from the right.

items.q: Which toy is 3rd from the right?
items.e: Start at the right end. Count 1, 2, 3: the star, the beaver, the apple. The 3rd toy is the apple. The duck is 3rd from the left.

items.q: Which toy is 4th from the left?
items.e: Start at the left end. Count 1, 2, 3, 4: the cat, the teddy, the apple, the ball. The 4th toy is the ball. The teddy is 4th from the right.

items.q: Which toy is 2nd from the right?
items.e: Start at the right end. Count 1, 2: the ball, the teddy. The 2nd toy is the teddy. The star is 2nd from the left.

items.q: What is just to the right of the beaver?
items.e: Find the beaver. Look to the right side of it. The toy just to the right is the book. The cat is on the other side.

items.q: What is just to the left of the apple?
items.e: Find the apple. Look to the left side of it. The toy just to the left is the car. The teddy is on the other side.

items.q: What is just to the left of the mitt?
items.e: Find the mitt. Look to the left side of it. The toy just to the left is the teddy. The cat is on the other side.

items.q: What is just to the right of the duck?
items.e: Find the duck. Look to the right side of it. The toy just to the right is the star. The book is on the other side.

items.q: Where is the beaver?
c: to the left of the ball
to the right of the ball
items.e: The beaver is on the left side of the ball. So it is to the left of the ball.

items.q: Where is the car?
c: to the right of the star
to the left of the star
items.e: The car is on the right side of the star. So it is to the right of the star.

items.q: Where is the cat?
c: to the left of the teddy
to the right of the teddy
items.e: The cat is on the left side of the teddy. So it is to the left of the teddy.

items.q: Which picture shows the beaver to the left of the ball?
items.e: Picture C. The beaver is on the left side. The ball is on the right side.

items.q: Which picture shows the duck to the right of the star?
items.e: Picture B. The star is on the left side. The duck is on the right side.

items.q: The car is 1st from the left. What is it from the right?
items.e: Start at the right end: duck 1st, apple 2nd, mitt 3rd, car 4th.

sets.title: Follow moves on a grid: 2 squares right, then 1 up

items.q: The beaver goes 3 squares right. Where does it stop?
items.e: Do not count the beaver’s own square. Go right: 1, 2, 3. It stops on the puck. Going the wrong way gets to the star.

items.q: The beaver goes 3 squares left. Where does it stop?
items.e: Do not count the beaver’s own square. Go left: 1, 2, 3. It stops on the duck. Counting the beaver’s square stops on the teddy.

items.q: The beaver goes 2 squares up. Where does it stop?
items.e: Do not count the beaver’s own square. Go up: 1, 2. It stops on the cat. Counting the beaver’s square stops on the mitt.

items.q: The beaver goes 2 squares down. Where does it stop?
items.e: Do not count the beaver’s own square. Go down: 1, 2. It stops on the star. Counting the beaver’s square stops on the duck.

items.q: The beaver goes 2 squares left. Where does it stop?
items.e: Do not count the beaver’s own square. Go left: 1, 2. It stops on the star. Going the wrong way gets to the mitt.

items.q: The beaver goes 1 square up. Where does it stop?
items.e: Do not count the beaver’s own square. Go up: 1. It stops on the apple. Going the wrong way gets to the mitt.

items.q: How many squares right to get to the apple?
items.e: Do not count the beaver’s own square. Count each move: 1, 2, 3, 4. That is 4.

items.q: How many squares left to get to the duck?
items.e: Do not count the beaver’s own square. Count each move: 1, 2, 3. That is 3.

items.q: How many squares up to get to the teddy?
items.e: Do not count the beaver’s own square. Count each move: 1, 2, 3. That is 3.

items.q: The beaver goes 2 squares right, then 1 square up. Where does it stop?
items.e: Do not count the beaver’s own square. Go right: 1, 2. Go up: 1. It stops on the duck. Counting the beaver’s square stops on the cat.

items.q: The beaver goes 3 squares right, then 2 squares up. Where does it stop?
items.e: Do not count the beaver’s own square. Go right: 1, 2, 3. Go up: 1, 2. It stops on the teddy. Counting the beaver’s square stops on the cat.

items.q: The beaver goes 2 squares left, then 2 squares up. Where does it stop?
items.e: Do not count the beaver’s own square. Go left: 1, 2. Go up: 1, 2. It stops on the duck. Counting the beaver’s square stops on the puck.

items.q: The beaver goes 3 squares left, then 2 squares down. Where does it stop?
items.e: Do not count the beaver’s own square. Go left: 1, 2, 3. Go down: 1, 2. It stops on the puck. Counting the beaver’s square stops on the duck.

items.q: The beaver goes 2 squares down, then 3 squares right. Where does it stop?
items.e: Do not count the beaver’s own square. Go down: 1, 2. Go right: 1, 2, 3. It stops on the teddy. Counting the beaver’s square stops on the mitt.

items.q: The beaver goes 3 squares down, then 2 squares left. Where does it stop?
items.e: Do not count the beaver’s own square. Go down: 1, 2, 3. Go left: 1, 2. It stops on the apple. Going the wrong way gets to the duck.

items.q: The beaver goes 1 square right, then 2 squares down. Where does it stop?
items.e: Do not count the beaver’s own square. Go right: 1. Go down: 1, 2. It stops on the mitt. Going the wrong way gets to the cat.

items.q: Which moves take the beaver to the teddy?
items.e: Do not count the beaver’s own square. Count the moves: 2 squares right, then 1 square up.

items.q: Which moves take the beaver to the mitt?
items.e: Do not count the beaver’s own square. Count the moves: 3 squares left, then 2 squares up.

items.q: Which moves take the beaver to the ball?
items.e: Do not count the beaver’s own square. Count the moves: 3 squares right, then 2 squares down.

items.q: Which moves take the beaver to the star?
items.e: Do not count the beaver’s own square. Count the moves: 4 squares left, then 1 square up.

sets.title: Which way to the carpet? Directions on a classroom map

items.q: Which way does Maya go to get to the carpet?
items.e: Go down. Do not count Maya’s own square. Count 1, 2. That is 2 squares down.

items.q: Which way does Liam go to get to the sink?
items.e: Go right. Do not count Liam’s own square. Count 1, 2, 3. That is 3 squares right.

items.q: Which way does Zoe go to get to the plant?
items.e: Go down. Do not count Zoe’s own square. Count 1, 2. That is 2 squares down.

items.q: Which way does Owen go to get to the easel?
items.e: Go right. Do not count Owen’s own square. Count 1, 2. That is 2 squares right.

items.q: Which way does Priya go to get to the carpet?
items.e: Go left. Do not count Priya’s own square. Count 1. That is 1 square left.

items.q: Which way does Kai go to get to the carpet?
items.e: First go 2 squares right. Then go 1 square down. Count the moves, not Kai’s own square.

items.q: Which way does Hana go to get to the easel?
items.e: First go 3 squares right. Then go 1 square up. Count the moves, not Hana’s own square.

items.q: Which way does Noah go to get to the door?
items.e: First go 4 squares left. Then go 1 square up. Count the moves, not Noah’s own square.

items.q: Which way does Amira go to get to the plant?
items.e: First go 3 squares right. Then go 1 square down. Count the moves, not Amira’s own square.

items.q: Which way does Lucas go to get to the coats?
items.e: First go 3 squares left. Then go 1 square down. Count the moves, not Lucas’s own square.

items.q: Mei goes 1 square left, then 1 square up. Where is she now?
items.e: Go 1 square left then 1 square up. Mei gets to the door.

items.q: Ethan goes 2 squares right, then 1 square down. Where is he now?
items.e: Go 2 squares right then 1 square down. Ethan gets to the plant.

items.q: Chloe goes 1 square up, then 1 square right. Where is she now?
items.e: Go 1 square up then 1 square right. Chloe gets to the shelf.

items.q: Mateo goes 2 squares right. Where is he now?
items.e: Go 2 squares right. Mateo gets to the sink.

items.q: Leah goes 1 square left. Where is she now?
items.e: Go 1 square left. Leah gets to the easel.

items.q: What is just to the left of the desk?
items.e: Look at the desk. The square on its left side has the plant. The sink is above the desk.

items.q: What is just above the desk?
items.e: Look up from the desk. The sink is in the square above it.

items.q: What is in the top right corner?
items.e: Top is the top row. Right is the side of your right hand. The shelf is there. The door is top left.

items.q: How many squares does Ava move to the right to get to the sink?
items.e: Do not count Ava’s own square. Count 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. That is 5 squares.

items.q: How many squares does Arjun move to the right to get to the carpet?
items.e: The carpet is in the very next square. That is 1 square.

sets.title: Word problems: lines, cubbies and the way to the rink

items.q: The class lines up at the gym door. Who is just behind Maya?
items.e: Behind Maya means further from the door. That is Owen. Liam is in front of Maya.

items.q: Who is just in front of Zoe?
items.e: In front of Zoe means closer to the door. That is Owen. Arjun is behind Zoe.

items.q: How many children are in front of Owen?
items.e: Liam and Maya are in front of Owen. That is 2. Do not count Owen.

items.q: The class sits on the carpet. Who sits just to the right of Noah?
items.e: Find Noah. Look to the right side. Emma is next. Mei is on Noah’s left side.

items.q: Who sits between Emma and Leah?
items.e: Emma is on one side. Leah is on the other side. Kai is in the middle.

items.q: Where does Mei sit?
items.e: Mei is the first child on the left side. She sits at the left end.

items.q: Each child puts winter boots in a cubby. Whose cubby is just above Ava’s?
items.e: Find Ava’s cubby. Look straight up. It is Owen’s. Noah’s and Kai’s are beside it.

items.q: Whose cubby is just below Zoe’s?
items.e: Find Zoe’s cubby. Look straight down. It is Noah’s.

items.q: Whose cubby is just to the right of Kai’s?
items.e: Find Kai’s cubby. Look to the right side. It is Ava’s. Mei’s is on the left side.

items.q: Ethan is at home. He walks 4 squares right. Where is he?
items.e: Do not count the home square. Count 1, 2, 3, 4. Ethan is at the school. 5 squares would be the rink.

items.q: Sofia is at the library. She walks 2 squares left to skate. Where is she?
items.e: Do not count the library square. Count 1, 2 to the left. Sofia is at the rink.

items.q: How many squares is it from home to the school?
items.e: Do not count the home square. Count the moves: 1, 2, 3, 4. That is 4.

items.q: Jayden is at the rink. Which way does he go to get to the store?
items.e: The store is on the left side of the rink. Count the moves: 1, 2, 3. That is 3 squares left.

items.q: Olivia wants the toy on the middle shelf, just to the right of the beaver. What does she get?
items.e: The middle shelf has the mitt, the beaver and the apple. Just to the right of the beaver is the apple.

items.q: Aiden puts away the puck. What is just above the puck?
items.e: The puck is on the bottom shelf. Look up one shelf. The apple is there. The cat is beside the puck.

items.q: The beaver goes 2 squares right. How many squares up to get to the star now?
items.e: After 2 squares right, the star is straight up. Count 1, 2, 3. That is 3.

items.q: Kai takes 3 steps forward. Then he takes 3 steps back. Where is he now?
items.e: 3 steps forward and 3 steps back cancel out. Kai is back where he started.

items.q: Zoe stands in front of Lucas in a line. Where is Lucas?
items.e: If Zoe is in front of Lucas, then Lucas is behind Zoe.

items.q: Nathan walks 3 squares up. Then he walks 2 squares right. How many squares does he walk in all?
items.e: Add the moves: 3 + 2 = 5. Do not count the square he starts on.

items.q: Emma says, “Go 2 squares right, then 1 square up.” Liam goes 2 squares left, then 1 square up. What did Liam mix up?
items.e: Emma said right. Liam went left. He mixed up left and right. The up move was correct.
